decisions.reason: SOL preserves the slow slide and heat while naturally rendering the shadows passing overhead.
SOL keeps the scream-like cries without changing their meaning.
SOL preserves the skeletal wings and vivid blue eyes in natural prose.
“Gaze” naturally carries the undead eyes’ ominous light in context.
“Something caught between life and death” keeps the source’s image.

SOL combines the lack of fear with the already-known fact that the undead are not enemies; the following deletions avoid repetition.

The undead-monsters point is retained in H007, so this deletion avoids repetition.
“On their side” naturally preserves that the creatures’ master is an ally.

“I’m done” naturally conveys the speaker’s refusal to continue.
SOL keeps the insult and comparison while avoiding the redundant “like you use.”

SOL retains the vibrations crumbling the dunes in a more direct sentence.

“Build suspense” keeps the deadpan joke.
“Yes” is a natural affirmative with no change in meaning.
The fragment “An enormous army” preserves the emphasis without the redundant setup.
SOL preserves that ten thousand is only a confirmed minimum and the true number may be higher.

SOL preserves the Hunters’ fear of death in natural phrasing.
SOL keeps the intensifying vibrations and trembling gaze as the sand shifts.

SOL retains the image of comrades or themselves dying amid blood and battle.

SOL naturally preserves Jin’s knowledge from the day he survived alone through the present.

SOL carries the question and the “everyone wondered, but no one knew” framing together.
“Some inkling” naturally preserves a vague idea.

SOL preserves the contrast between the Hunters’ blood and the monsters’ as the heat stirs them.

The tighter phrasing preserves the heat’s warping effect.
SOL keeps the spearhead blazing like a blue-white sun in the sunlight.
“Came free” naturally describes weapons being drawn.
SOL preserves the vehicles moving into position to block the front.
The sentence retains the steel wall taking shape amid heavy thuds.
SOL keeps the advancing monster wave and the vast cloud of sand.
SOL preserves Jin watching the monsters and the surprising matter-of-fact delivery.

SOL retains the initial burst of laughter, the Hunter’s reaction, and the group’s laughter.

The thought that it would sound absurd is retained in H071, so this deletion avoids repetition.
SOL changes the ungendered “they” to “him,” adding an unsupported gender.

SOL preserves the swelling noise and the Hunters’ inability to stop laughing.
SOL retains Jin standing mountain-like on the dune and swinging his spear.

The complete sentence preserves the battle’s opening and later name.
“Still burning down” naturally preserves the cigar’s continued slow burn.
SOL keeps the gift’s source and value without changing the meaning.
